History: The Lubim, or Libyans, appear as warriors of the North African coast west of Egypt. They marched with Shishak against Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 12:3) and are named among Egypt's allies (2 Chronicles 16:8; Nahum 3:9). Ezekiel lists Libya among the peoples falling with Egypt (Ezekiel 30:5) and among Gog's allies (Ezekiel 38:5), and Libyans were present at Pentecost (Acts 2:10). The Lehabim of Genesis 10:13 are traditionally identified with these Libyans.
Culture: Libyans were semi-nomadic herders and warriors of the coastal tribes, serving as soldiers and charioteers in Egyptian and other Near Eastern armies.
Religion: Libyans shared much of Egypt's religious world, worshipping Libyan and Egyptian deities of the desert and the Nile valley.
BibleConnection: Libya's biblical role is chiefly as Egypt's western neighbor and ally, named in judgment oracles and, at Pentecost, among the nations hearing the gospel in their own tongue.
KeyScriptures: 2 Chronicles 12:3; 2 Chronicles 16:8; Nahum 3:9; Ezekiel 30:5; Ezekiel 38:5; Acts 2:10
